newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca says Arimidex extends cancer survival.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca says Arimidex extends cancer survival.

text.p: Zeneca Pharmaceuticals said its advanced breast cancer drug Arimidex gave patients a "significant survival benefit" over those treated with megestrol acetate in randomised clinical trials. "Zeneca believes that it now has a product which is not only better tolerated but has shown a significant survival advantage over megestrol acetate, a widely used standard therapy," the company said in a statement. Arimidex (anastrozole) was the first of a new generation of drugs known as aromatase inhibitors, which suppress the hormone oestrogen in hormone-responsive breast cancer.

It was considered somewhat less effective than megestrol acetate, but offering the convenience of once-daily dosing and improved tolerability. Zeneca said its study, which it says will be published as soon as possible in the medical literature, argued against this perception.
Zeneca is the second largest maker of oncology drugs after Bristol-Myers Squibb.
Ciba-Geigy AG also makes an aromatase inhibitor -- Femara (letrozole).
Arimidex is approved in Britain, the United States, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, Italy, Austria, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Finland, Sweden and Switzerland.
